h1: The 6 Best Combination Laptop Locks of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Combination Laptop Locks: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 6 best combination laptop locks for 2026, sorted by slot type, cable length and recovery options, with who each suits.
summary: The Kensington Universal 3-in-1 2.0 is the best combination laptop lock, with interchangeable Standard, Nano and Wedge tips on a rotatable head. The older Kensington universal model has a 6 ft cut-resistant cable and code recovery. The T-Bar, NanoSaver and N17 Dell locks suit single slot types, and the Multplx audio-port anchor serves laptops with no slot at all.
intro: A combination laptop lock does nothing if it does not fit the slot. Standard, Nano and Wedge slots look like cousins and are not interchangeable, and that mismatch is the leading reason these locks come back in the box. Before you compare anything else, look at the edge of your laptop and identify which slot it has, or whether it has one at all.

Six combination locks went through our spec-sheet review here, and slot coverage, cable length, code reset and recovery, and warranty set the order on the Primea score. Prices are buckets only. No lock makes a laptop theft-proof, so treat every pick as a deterrent that slows an opportunist down and protects a desk in a shared space.

products.name: Kensington Universal 3-in-1 2.0 Combination Laptop Lock, K63394WW
products.verdict: One lock with swappable tips for Standard, Nano and Wedge slots.
products.description:
This Kensington ships with interchangeable Standard, Nano and N17 Wedge tips and a resettable 4-digit dial with 10,000 combinations. The head rotates 360 degrees, in the $25 to $50 bucket. A rotating head stops the cable from twisting against the laptop edge, which is where thin ports tend to loosen under strain.

It ranks first because it covers the three common slot types in one package, so it fits a laptop you buy next year. The older universal model has a longer cable, but this version adds the rotating head.

Buy it for mixed-brand homes and small offices. The caveats are that tips can get lost and that it does not work on slotless laptops. Skip it if you own one laptop with a known slot.
products.skipIf: You own a single laptop with a known slot.

products.name: Kensington Universal 3-in-1 Combination Laptop Lock, K62316WW
products.verdict: The earlier universal model, with a longer 6 ft cut-resistant cable.
products.description:
This version has tethered Standard, Nano and Wedge tips, a 6 ft cut-resistant cable and a Register and Retrieve option to recover a forgotten code, in the $25 to $50 bucket. Tethered tips stay attached to the lock, so the one you are not using cannot wander off.

It ranks just below the 2.0 because the 2.0 adds a rotatable head, while this one wins on cable reach and code recovery. Against the single-slot locks, it still covers every common port.

Buy it for shared desks that need cable reach, where a forgotten code is a real risk. The caveats are a bulkier tip system and no help for slotless laptops. Skip it if your laptop has no security slot.
products.idealFor: Shared desks that need cable reach.
products.skipIf: Your laptop has no security slot.

products.name: Kensington Combination Cable T-Bar Standard Lock, K64673AM
products.verdict: A simple, proven lock for laptops with a Standard slot.
products.description:
This Kensington lock uses a resettable 4-wheel dial with 10,000 combinations and fits the Standard T-Bar slot only. It lists independent torque and pull testing by Kensington, in the $25 to $50 bucket. A tested lock gives you evidence of strength, which most cheap cables never offer.

It ranks third because it covers just one slot, unlike the universal models, and costs about the same. If you know you own a Standard-slot laptop, though, its simple dial is all you need.

Buy it for owners of laptops with a Standard slot. The caveats are the single slot type and a price above a basic lock. Skip it if you use Dell, Nano or slotless machines, where it will not seat.
products.skipIf: You use Dell, Nano or slotless laptops.

products.name: Kensington NanoSaver Combination Laptop Lock, K60603WW
products.verdict: Nano-slot lock with online code recovery and a 2-year warranty.
products.description:
The NanoSaver fits the Nano slot on select HP, Lenovo and Asus models. It has a resettable 4-wheel dial, online code recovery and a 2-year warranty with lifetime technical support, in the $25 to $50 bucket. Nano slots are thinner than Standard ones, so a dedicated lock seats more securely than a tip adapter.

It ranks fourth because it is slot-specific and the compatibility list is narrow. The warranty and online recovery are better than the T-Bar lock's, but the fit is more restrictive.

Buy it if you own a compatible Nano-slot laptop and tend to forget codes. The caveats are the Nano slot only and select models. Skip it if your laptop uses a Standard slot.
products.skipIf: Your laptop uses a Standard slot.

products.name: Kensington N17 Dell Laptop Combination Lock, K68008WW
products.verdict: The Wedge-slot lock for 2016-and-newer Dell and Alienware.
products.description:
The N17 Dell lock fits the Dell and Alienware Wedge slot and uses a tapered wedge that engages under tension. The dial is resettable with 10,000 combinations, in the under $25 bucket. A wedge that tightens as you pull on the cable resists being yanked out.

It ranks fifth only because it is the narrowest fit here. For Dell owners it is the cheapest dedicated option, and it undercuts the universal models. No code recovery is listed, so you must remember the code.

Buy it for 2016-and-newer Dell and Alienware laptops. The caveats are the Dell-only fit and no recovery option. Skip it if your laptop is not Dell or Alienware.
products.skipIf: Your laptop is not Dell or Alienware.

products.name: Multplx Universal Laptop Security Lock, Audio Port Anchor
products.verdict: An audio-port anchor kit for laptops with no security slot.
products.description:
This kit anchors through the audio port and includes a 1.7m cable and a resettable 4-digit combination lock. It lists use across multiple audio-port-equipped devices, not just Apple, in the $25 to $50 bucket. For ultrabooks and MacBooks that have no security slot, a port anchor is the only cable route.

It ranks last because an audio port anchor is a different security class from a slot lock: it relies on the port and the anchor, not a reinforced steel notch. It still deters casual theft, which is its purpose.

Buy it for slotless laptops. The caveats are that it needs an audio port and is not a slot lock. Skip it if your laptop has a security slot, because the Kensington locks are sturdier.
products.skipIf: Your laptop has a security slot.

whatMatters.detail: Standard, Nano and Wedge slots differ in shape, and a lock for one will not seat in another. Match the slot to avoid returns. Look at the port's shape, or check your laptop model in the maker's compatibility list, and note that some thin laptops have no slot at all. Ten seconds with a flashlight beats a return shipment.

A short cable limits where you can anchor, while a longer one reaches a table leg. Around 5 to 6 ft covers most desks, and the older Kensington universal lists 6 ft. Check the listed length rather than assuming, and think about whether you will loop around a desk, a pipe or a heavy fixture. Cable reach matters more than people expect.

A resettable dial lets you pick a code you remember and change it if shared. A forgotten code can lock you out. Look for resettable and any recovery service on the listing, such as Register and Retrieve or online recovery, and write the code somewhere safe before you rely on the lock. A forgotten code is a bigger risk than a thief.

A cable is only as good as what it wraps around. A heavy desk or fixed pipe works, while a light chair does not. Plan where you will loop it before buying, and make sure the loop cannot slip off a table leg, since an easy slip defeats the whole lock. Loop it around something that cannot be lifted off.

Warranty and support show the maker stands behind the lock. Only a few listings state terms, such as the NanoSaver's 2-year warranty and lifetime technical support. Check the warranty length in the bullet points, and favor makers that publish it, since an unstated warranty usually means a short one. Support matters when a dial jams.

faq.q: How do I know my slot type?
faq.a: Look at the port on the laptop edge and compare it with the maker's pictures. Your model's spec page often names the slot, and the Kensington universal locks include all three tip types if you are unsure, so you do not have to guess before ordering.

faq.q: Will a combination lock stop a determined thief?
faq.a: No lock is theft-proof. It deters opportunistic theft and slows others down. A Kensington cable plus an alert owner is the practical defense. Lock it every time, not only in cafes.

faq.q: Is a universal lock worth it?
faq.a: Yes if you own different laptops. For a single known slot a dedicated lock like the T-Bar or Dell model costs less and has fewer parts to lose.

faq.q: How do I set the code?
faq.a: Follow the maker's reset steps in the instructions, then test it several times before relying on it. Keep a note of the new code.

Most MacBooks lack a slot, so you need an adapter or a port-based anchor. The Multplx audio-port kit lists use across multiple devices, so check its compatibility and that your laptop has a standard audio port.

faq.q: What if I forget the code?
faq.a: Some locks offer online recovery or registration, like the NanoSaver and older universal model. Others need you to contact support, so note your code and keep it private, since a lock is only as secret as its code.

finalTake: Buy the Kensington 2.0 if you own mixed laptops or are unsure of the slot, and the older universal model if you want the longer cable and code recovery. Pick the dedicated T-Bar, NanoSaver or Dell lock if you know your slot and want a simpler tool. Use the Multplx anchor only for slotless laptops, and expect a different kind of protection.
